verification_results.data_rights_success_text_sample: Request received. Reference: bbeeb254 — We will respond by 6/27/2026 at the latest.
verification_results.delete_cancel_flow_ui_elements_present: all 4 (privacy-delete-confirm, privacy-delete-btn, privacy-delete-scheduled, privacy-cancel-delete) confirmed on Pro Privacy tab; backend roundtrip PASSES in test_deletion_schedule_and_cancel_roundtrip

observations_and_minor_findings: Documentation mismatch (NOT a bug): the review_request lists [data-testid=tab-privacy] but actual implementation uses role-prefixed testids — `pro-settings-tab-privacy` (ProSettingsPage.jsx:275) for Pro and `settings-tab-privacy` (SettingsPage.jsx:81) for Homeowner. This matches the existing convention (settings-tab-* / pro-settings-tab-*) and is internally consistent. Suggest the main agent either (a) update the review_request testid spec to the role-prefixed names OR (b) add an additional `tab-privacy` alias if cross-role tooling is expected.

/data-rights success card does not literally print the word "30" or "days"; it shows an absolute response deadline (e.g., "We will respond by 6/27/2026 at the latest") which is the 30-day SLA expressed as a calendar date. Backend due_at field carries the +30d ISO timestamp. UX-wise this is clear; only flag if a stricter literal "30 days" copy is required.

End-to-end browser click of the throwaway delete→schedule→cancel UI flow was not completed in this iteration due to onboarding flow + test-environment cookie persistence (the new throwaway lands on /onboarding instead of /auth on the 2nd context). HOWEVER: (1) all 4 delete-flow testids render correctly on the Pro Privacy tab, and (2) the backend delete+cancel roundtrip PASSES (test_iter17_privacy.py::TestMeEndpoints::test_deletion_schedule_and_cancel_roundtrip). Main agent can self-test by manually clicking the flow.
action_items: (optional, doc nit) Reconcile testid naming: spec says `tab-privacy`, code uses `pro-settings-tab-privacy` / `settings-tab-privacy`. Either update the iter17 spec or add the unprefixed alias.
(optional, copy nit) Consider also showing the literal "30 days" string in the /data-rights success card alongside the absolute deadline date, for GDPR-clarity / SLA expectations.
